labels.name: comp/agent

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main

items.body:
### Bug Description

When using an auxiliary model (e.g., `auxiliary.compression`) configured with a model from a `custom_providers` entry, Hermes ignores the `context_length` explicitly set in the custom provider's model config and falls back to the model catalog's default value instead.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Define a custom provider with a model that has an explicit `context_length`:

```yaml
custom_providers:
  - name: aiclient2api-gemini-cli
    base_url: http://aiclient2api:3000/gemini-cli-oauth/v1
    api_key: sk-...
    models:
      gemini-3-flash-preview:
        context_length: 1048576   # 1M tokens
```

2. Configure an auxiliary task (e.g., compression) to use that model:

```yaml
auxiliary:
  compression:
    provider: aiclient2api-gemini-cli
    model: gemini-3-flash-preview
```

3. Start a Hermes session. Observe the warning:

> ⚠ Compression model gemini-3-flash-preview (aiclient2api-gemini-cli) context is 256,000 tokens, but the main model deepseek-v4-flash (opencode-go)'s compression threshold was 750,000 tokens. Auto-lowered this session's threshold to 256,000 tokens so compression can run.
>
> To make this permanent, edit config.yaml — either:
> 1. Use a larger compression model: ...
> 2. Lower the compression threshold: ...

### Expected Behavior

Hermes should read `context_length: 1048576` from `custom_providers[].models["gemini-3-flash-preview"].context_length` and use that value, instead of falling back to the model catalog default (256K).

### Actual Behavior

The custom provider's `context_length` is ignored. Hermes falls back to its internal model catalog, which has `gemini-3-flash-preview` listed with a default context of 256,000 tokens.

### Root Cause Analysis

The provider API (`GET /models`) returns no `context_length`/`context_window` field in its model metadata:

```json
{
  "data": [{
    "id": "gemini-3-flash-preview",
    "object": "model",
    "created": 1778873371,
    "owned_by": "google",
    "display_name": "Gemini 3 Flash Preview"
    // ← no context_length field
  }]
}
```

When Hermes resolves `context_length` for an auxiliary model, it appears to:
1. Query the provider API for model metadata → gets no context_length
2. Fall back to the model catalog → uses default (256K)
3. **Skip** the `custom_providers[].models[].context_length` configuration entirely

This contrasts with the main model (`model.default`), which correctly picks up context_length — suggesting the resolution path for `auxiliary.*` models differs from the main model's resolution path.

### Additional Context

- The main model (`model.default`) with the same provider resolves context_length correctly (1M), confirming the config is syntactically valid.
- `custom_providers[].models[].context_length` is the designated place to override context length when the provider doesn't advertise it via API.
- The bug affects all `auxiliary.*` tasks (compression, session_search, vision, web_extract, etc.) when using custom provider models.

### Suggested Fix

In the auxiliary model context_length resolution logic, before falling back to the model catalog, check if the model is defined under a `custom_providers` entry and use its `context_length` value if present.

### Actual Behavior

⚠ Compression model gemini-3-flash-preview (XXX provider) context is 256,000 tokens, but the main model deepseek-v4-flash (YYY provider)'s compression threshold was 750,000 tokens. Auto-lowered this session's threshold to 256,000 tokens so compression can run.
  To make this permanent, edit config.yaml — either:
  1. Use a larger compression model:
       auxiliary:
         compression:
           model: <model-with-750,000+-context>
  2. Lower the compression threshold:
       compression:
         threshold: 0.25

items.title: hermes_tools_mcp_server: scope docstring claims memory/session_search/delegate_task but EXPOSED_TOOLS excludes them

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## Summary

The Hermes-tools MCP server that backs the `codex_app_server` runtime
(`agent/transports/hermes_tools_mcp_server.py`) **claims** to expose
`memory`, `session_search`, `delegate_task`, and `text_to_speech` in its
top-of-file docstring, but the `EXPOSED_TOOLS` tuple a few lines later
deliberately **excludes** `memory`, `session_search`, `delegate_task`,
and `todo`.

A Codex session running under this runtime therefore sees Hermes' web,
browser, vision, image-gen, skills, kanban, and TTS tools, but has no
memory save/recall API, no cross-session search, no subagent delegation,
and no shared todo state — even when running under a Hermes profile
whose stored `MEMORY.md` / `USER.md` are accessible on disk.

This is a documentation/implementation contradiction at minimum, and a
real capability gap at most: in the default Hermes runtime an agent can
save a fact (`memory.add(...)`) and recall it next session. The same
profile run with `openai_runtime: codex_app_server` cannot.

## Where it is

`agent/transports/hermes_tools_mcp_server.py`

Docstring (lines ~1–34) — "Scope (what we expose)" lists:

> - `delegate_task` — Hermes subagents
> - `memory` — Hermes' persistent memory store
> - `session_search` — cross-session search
> - `text_to_speech` — TTS

Code, immediately below (lines ~44–58 of the inline comment, then
`EXPOSED_TOOLS` ~60–97):

```python
#   - delegate_task / memory / session_search / todo — these are
#     `_AGENT_LOOP_TOOLS` in Hermes (model_tools.py:493). They require
#     the running AIAgent context to dispatch (mid-loop state), so a
#     stateless MCP callback can't drive them. Hermes' default runtime
#     keeps these working; the codex_app_server runtime cannot.
EXPOSED_TOOLS: tuple[str, ...] = (
    "web_search",
    "web_extract",
    # browser / vision / image / skills / TTS / kanban only
    ...
)
```

`model_tools.py:484` confirms `_AGENT_LOOP_TOOLS = {"todo", "memory", "session_search", "delegate_task"}` — the dispatcher returns
`"<tool> must be handled by the agent loop"` if anything routes them through `handle_function_call()` from outside `AIAgent`.

`text_to_speech` is also docstring-listed but IS in `EXPOSED_TOOLS` — so
that one is correct, just stale in the prose.

## Why it matters

Repro pattern that surfaced this:

1. Hermes profile `hermes-codex` with `~/.hermes/profiles/hermes-codex/memories/MEMORY.md` and `USER.md` populated.
2. `~/.codex/config.toml` has `[mcp_servers.hermes-tools]` pointing at `agent/transports/hermes_tools_mcp_server.py`.
3. A Codex session in that profile (Codex-running-as-Hermes-Codex-bot in our Discord deployment) is asked whether it has memory access. It can read memory files via filesystem tools and lists what the MCP server actually advertises, and reports back: "no callable memory tool exposed."

That answer is correct given the code, but it contradicts what the docstring tells contributors the runtime should provide, and contradicts the cross-runtime parity expectation set by PR #24182 ("memory + skill nudges: yes (via item projection)" in the trade-off table). Whether `_AGENT_LOOP_TOOLS` should remain agent-loop-only is a separate architectural question; the immediate problem is that the file claims the tools are exposed when they are not.

## What I'd expect

One of the following, in order of escalating effort:

1. **Doc fix (minimum):** correct the top-of-file scope docstring to match `EXPOSED_TOOLS`. Remove `delegate_task` / `memory` / `session_search` from the "what we expose" list; the inline comment block already explains why. This stops misleading future contributors.

2. **Shim memory + session_search through a callback into the parent AIAgent.** `memory` and `session_search` both have legitimate stateless implementations — `session_search` reads `SessionDB` (see #105 for the parallel gateway fix; `session_db` only needs to be passed in), and `memory` reads/writes the profile's MEMORY.md/USER.md files under a lock. The "needs agent-loop state" rationale applies most strongly to `delegate_task` (which actually spawns nested AIAgent loops) and `todo` (which is per-loop UX state). The other two could plausibly be exposed via a thin wrapper that takes `HERMES_HOME` from env (already set on the MCP subprocess) and routes through `MemoryStore` / `SessionDB` directly, without an AIAgent.

3. **Full parity (most work):** keep memory/session_search agent-loop-only, but plumb the parent AIAgent's memory store and session DB through the MCP callback as a side channel so the tools work transparently from the codex runtime. Similar in spirit to #105's gateway fix.

## Related

- **#26035** — codex_app_server does not receive Hermes SOUL / system prompt / assembled memory context. Different problem (input *context* injection vs. *tool* exposure) but the same runtime and same impact on persona-sensitive profiles. Worth coordinating fixes.
- **#10835** — external `hermes mcp serve` (the `mcp_serve.py` for Claude Code / Cursor) also doesn't expose memory, with implementation proposed in #10833. That server is separate from the `hermes-tools` MCP this issue covers, but a unified `MemoryStore`-over-MCP wrapper could potentially serve both.
- **#105** (closed) — the gateway-side analog where `session_search` was unreachable because the gateway didn't pass `session_db` to `AIAgent`. Same shape of fix may apply here.
- **PR #24182** — introduced the codex_app_server runtime with the trade-off table that claimed memory parity.

## Caveats

I haven't audited whether the `MemoryStore` / `SessionDB` interfaces are
genuinely safe to invoke from a forked MCP subprocess (file locking
across processes, plugin-provided memory backends like Honcho/mem0 that
may assume in-process state, etc.). The doc-only fix (option 1) is
safe; options 2 and 3 want a careful look at the plugin memory paths in
`plugins/memory/` first.

items.title: [Feature]: Persist /model selections per chat/thread across gateway restarts

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Problem

`/model <name>` in the gateway stores the selection in
`GatewayRunner._session_model_overrides` (in-memory dict). Per-thread
selections are lost on gateway restart, and threads revert to `model.default`.

`/model <name> --global` is durable but changes the default for *all* threads,
defeating per-thread use.

## Use case

Pin different threads to different models (e.g. fast model in one thread,
flagship in another, vision-capable in a third) and have those selections
survive gateway restarts — without spinning up a separate profile per model
(which requires its own config, .env, bot token, gateway process).

## Proposed solution

Persist `_session_model_overrides` (and likely `_session_reasoning_overrides`)
to SQLite/JSON under `~/.hermes/<profile>/state/`, keyed by `session_key`.
Load on gateway startup; write through on `/model`. Clear on session reset
(`/new`). `--global` continues to update `model.default` unchanged.

## Related

- #20249 — per-turn expert-on-demand model escalation (adjacent, different scope)
- #10688 — `/model` reliability in Slack (related, different scope)

## Code pointers

- `gateway/run.py:1162` — `_session_model_overrides` declaration
- `gateway/run.py:9096`, `8956` — write paths
- `hermes_state.py` — `SessionDB` is the likely home for persistence

items.title: [Bug] kanban dispatcher tick fails with "duplicate column name: max_retries" on legacy DB

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
### Bug Report

`_migrate_add_optional_columns` crashes the kanban dispatcher tick on legacy DBs:

```
ERROR gateway.run: kanban dispatcher: tick failed on board default
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/opt/hermes/gateway/run.py", line 3878, in _tick_once_for_board
    conn = _kb.connect(board=slug)
  File "/opt/hermes/hermes_cli/kanban_db.py", line 928, in connect
    _migrate_add_optional_columns(conn)
  File "/opt/hermes/hermes_cli/kanban_db.py", line 1034, in _migrate_add_optional_columns
    conn.execute("ALTER TABLE tasks ADD COLUMN max_retries INTEGER")
sqlite3.OperationalError: duplicate column name: max_retries
```

Reproduces on every gateway start when the DB already contains `max_retries` (from a prior upgrade or any path that ran `SCHEMA_SQL`'s `ALTER TABLE` before `_migrate_add_optional_columns` re-reads `PRAGMA table_info(tasks)`). The dispatcher recovers (the gateway keeps running) but every tick logs the same traceback, so logs are noisy and any error-budget / alerting setup goes red.

### Environment

- Image: `nousresearch/hermes-agent:v2026.5.7`
- `hermes --version`: `Hermes Agent v0.13.0 (2026.5.7)`
- Python 3.13.5
- Deployment: Kubernetes pod with a persistent `/opt/data` volume (so legacy `kanban.db` survives image upgrades)

### Root cause

`hermes_cli/kanban_db.py:962` reads `cols` once at function entry and the comment at line ~995 acknowledges the staleness explicitly:

```python
# NOTE: ``cols`` reflects the schema at entry to this function and is
# not refreshed between ALTER TABLE calls.  Every guard below checks
```

If any code path (concurrent process, prior partial migration, `SCHEMA_SQL` `executescript` in `connect()`) added `max_retries` after the `PRAGMA` snapshot was taken, the guard `if "max_retries" not in cols` reads stale and the `ALTER TABLE` re-fires.

### Existing PRs

Three PRs already proposed fixes for this exact path, all `closed` without merge:

- #22491 — `fix(kanban): defensive migration for duplicate max_retries column`
- #21874 — `fix(kanban): tolerate races on legacy-DB column migration`
- #21529 — `fix(kanban): make column migrations idempotent under concurrent access`

Could a maintainer share the position on why those were declined? Happy to redo a PR matching whatever approach is preferred — try/except around each `ALTER`, a `_safe_add_column()` helper, `PRAGMA` refresh between statements, or move to `ALTER TABLE … ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` (supported on SQLite ≥ 3.35, released 2021-03; well below Python 3.13's bundled libsqlite).

### Workaround (for anyone hitting this)

If your kanban board is empty / disposable, the DB will be recreated cleanly on next start:

```bash
# Optional backup
cp $HERMES_HOME/kanban.db $HERMES_HOME/kanban.db.bak
rm -f $HERMES_HOME/kanban.db $HERMES_HOME/kanban.db-wal $HERMES_HOME/kanban.db-shm
# Restart the gateway
```

If you have data you care about, hand-running `ALTER TABLE tasks ADD COLUMN max_retries INTEGER` once (or accepting that the migration already won the race) is enough — the column will then be detected on the next start and the migration skips it.

items.title: custom:<name> providers not recognized as aggregators (custom:zenmux)

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Describe the bug

Custom-named providers such as `custom:zenmux` are not recognized as multi-model aggregators in two places:

### 1. `hermes_cli/providers.py` — `is_aggregator()`
The function only returns `True` for providers registered in `PROVIDER_REGISTRY` that have `is_aggregator=True`. Custom-named providers like `custom:zenmux` fall through to `get_provider()` which returns `None` for unknown slugs, so `is_aggregator()` returns `False`.

This breaks model-alias resolution for vendor-prefixed model IDs (e.g. `google/gemini-3.1-flash-lite`) when the current provider is `custom:zenmux`.

### 2. `hermes_cli/doctor.py` — vendor-prefix validation
`hermes doctor` raises a false-positive warning:
```
model.default 'z-ai/glm-5.1' is vendor-prefixed but model.provider is 'custom:zenmux'.
Either set model.provider to 'openrouter', or drop the vendor prefix.
```
This is incorrect — `custom:zenmux` is an aggregator that accepts vendor-prefixed model slugs, just like `openrouter` or bare `custom`.

## Expected behavior
- `is_aggregator("custom:zenmux")` should return `True`
- `hermes doctor` should not warn about vendor-prefixed models when `model.provider` is `custom:<name>`

## Fix

**`hermes_cli/providers.py`**:
```python
def is_aggregator(provider: str) -> bool:
    if provider and provider.startswith("custom:"):
        return True
    pdef = get_provider(provider)
    return pdef.is_aggregator if pdef else False
```

**`hermes_cli/doctor.py`** — add `not provider_for_policy.startswith("custom:")` to the vendor-prefix check condition.

items.title: [Bug] Telegram Group Chat: Agent cannot see sender names / user identity

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Summary

In Telegram group chats, the agent receives messages without any indication of who sent them. This makes multi-user group conversations impossible to handle correctly — the agent cannot address users by name, attribute statements to speakers, or apply user-specific context.

**Critical distinction:** This is NOT about adding `[from NAME]` prefixes to message text (addressed in PR #13939 and PR #16850). This is about the **agent's core awareness of sender identity** in group chats, which works in some other agent implementations but not in Hermes.

## Environment

- **Hermes Agent version:** v2026.5.7+ (rolling release, updated 2026-05-12)
- **Platform:** Telegram
- **Chat type:** Group (supergroup with 3 participants)
- **Config:** `group_sessions_per_user: false` (shared session)
- **OS:** macOS 15.x (gateway runs locally)

## Expected Behavior

When multiple users participate in a Telegram group chat with the agent, the agent should be able to:
1. See who sent each message (user name / display name)
2. Address users by name in responses
3. Attribute statements to specific speakers
4. Apply user-specific memory/preferences

This works correctly in other agent implementations (e.g., OpenCode) running against the same Telegram Bot API.

## Actual Behavior

The agent receives messages in group chats **without any sender identity information**. The `source` object or session context does not contain the sender's display name or username. The agent sees only the raw message text.

Example from a group chat with users "Alice", "hermes_bot", and "Bob":

```
# What the agent sees:
"check the file notes.txt in the docs folder"

# What the agent SHOULD see:
"[from Alice] check the file notes.txt in the docs folder"
# OR the sender info should be available in source.user_name / source.display_name
```

The agent cannot determine whether the message came from "Alice", "Bob", or anyone else. This breaks:
- Personalized responses ("Got it, Alice" vs generic "Got it")
- User-specific memory application
- Multi-user attribution in shared sessions

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Add Hermes Agent bot to a Telegram group with multiple users
2. Ensure `group_sessions_per_user: false` in config (shared session mode)
3. Send messages from different users
4. Observe that the agent has no access to sender identity

## Related Issues and PRs

| Issue/PR | Description | Relevance |
|----------|-------------|-----------|
| PR #13939 | `feat(gateway): authoritative sender attribution in all chat contexts` | Adds `[from NAME (uid:ID)]` prefix to message text. Does NOT fix core sender visibility — it's a text-prefix workaround |
| PR #16850 | `fix(gateway/telegram): quoted-image vision, sender sidecars, reply prefix, multi-sender merge attribution` | Fixes sender attribution in busy-queue merges and reply contexts. Partial overlap but different scope |
| PR #22711 | `feat(gateway): inject user_id alongside display name in session context` | Adds user_id to session context prompt. Does not expose sender name per-message |
| Issue #15647 | `[WhatsApp] group_sessions_per_user splits agent's view` | WhatsApp-specific, different platform |

**None of the above resolve the core issue:** the Telegram gateway adapter does not populate sender identity fields that the agent can access in real-time during message processing.

## Proposed Solutions

### Option A: Populate `source.user_name` in Telegram adapter
Ensure the Telegram gateway adapter populates `source.user_name` (or equivalent field) with the sender's display name for EVERY inbound message, not just in certain modes.

### Option B: Expose sender in `SessionSource` metadata
Add sender information to the `SessionSource` object that is injected into the agent's context, so the agent can reference `source.sender_name` or similar.

### Option C: System prompt injection
Automatically inject a "Current speaker: NAME" line into the system prompt when processing group chat messages, updating it per-turn.

## Additional Context

- The Telegram Bot API **does** provide `from.first_name`, `from.last_name`, `from.username` in every `Update` object. This information is available at the gateway level.
- Other agent frameworks (tested: OpenCode) successfully extract and expose this information to the agent in the same group chat scenario.
- The issue persists regardless of `group_sessions_per_user` setting (tested both `true` and `false`).

## Checklist

- Hermes Agent: latest Docker image (nousresearch/hermes-agent)
- Platform: Telegram gateway
- Model: hermes3-alias (custom Ollama modelfile based on hermes3:latest)
- HERMES_HOME: /opt/data (volume mounted from host ~/.hermes-alias)

2. Set `agent.personality` in config.yaml to a custom named personality

4. Send a message via Telegram asking the agent who it is

Agent responds using SOUL.md content or the named personality defined in `agent.personalities`.

## Actual Behavior
Agent always responds as "I am Hermes Agent, an intelligent AI assistant created by Nous Research."

## Root Cause (identified)
In `run_agent.py`, `load_soul_identity` defaults to `False` and is never set to `True` when AIAgent is instantiated from the gateway. The condition on line 5835:

items.title: [Bug]: Codex backend rejects 'extra_headers' field in Responses payload (HTTP 400)

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
### Summary

`chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses` started rejecting the `extra_headers` field that Hermes injects into the Responses API payload, returning `HTTP 400 {"detail":"Unsupported parameter: extra_headers"}`. As a result, every primary call on `gpt-5.5` (and any other Codex-routed model) returns 400, falling through to the configured fallback provider on every chat message.

I noticed this start around **2026-05-15 ~16:00 UTC** — Hermes payload format wasn't changed; the Codex backend tightened body validation.

### Hermes version

- `hermes-agent` v0.13.0 (v2026.5.7)
- Container image: `ghcr.io/openclaw/openclaw:2026.5.12` running our `hermes-agent-template` fork
- Provider: `openai-codex` via OAuth (`hermes auth add openai-codex --type oauth`)
- Model: `gpt-5.5`

### Reproduction

1. Configure Codex OAuth: `hermes auth add openai-codex --type oauth`
2. Set Codex as primary: `hermes model` → choose OpenAI Codex → gpt-5.5
3. Send any message via gateway (Telegram, Discord, etc.) or `hermes -m gpt-5.5 --provider openai-codex -z "ping"`
4. Observe `Fallback activated: gpt-5.5 → <fallback>` in `agent.log` and `Primary model failed — switching to fallback` in the chat.

### Wire-level diagnosis

Enabled `HERMES_DUMP_REQUESTS=1`, captured a dumped preflight body, and replayed with `urllib` + raw access_token:

```python
# Hermes-shaped body (truncated)
body = {
    "model": "gpt-5.5",
    "instructions": "...",
    "input": [...],
    "store": False,
    "tools": [...],         # 77 functions
    "reasoning": {"effort": "medium", "summary": "auto"},
    "include": ["reasoning.encrypted_content"],
    "tool_choice": "auto",
    "parallel_tool_calls": True,
    "prompt_cache_key": "<session_id>",
    "extra_headers": {
        "session_id": "<session_id>",
        "x-client-request-id": "<session_id>"
    },
    "stream": True,
}
# POST to chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses with Authorization: Bearer <token>
# → HTTP 400 {"detail":"Unsupported parameter: extra_headers"}
```

After removing `extra_headers` from the body and resending (everything else identical):

```
→ HTTP 200, response.created event streaming back
```

### Source

`agent/transports/codex.py` (around payload assembly) and `agent/codex_responses_adapter.py::_preflight_codex_api_kwargs` both pass `extra_headers` through to the final body. It looks like the field is intended to become HTTP headers (and does on the regular OpenAI Responses API endpoint), but for the Codex-flavored backend it should be moved to the HTTP request headers level — or stripped if the SDK already sets the corresponding `x-client-request-id` header through another channel.

### Suggested fix

In `agent/codex_responses_adapter.py::_preflight_codex_api_kwargs` (or the request builder in `agent/transports/codex.py`), when `is_codex_backend=True`, lift `extra_headers` out of the body and into the HTTP request headers via the OpenAI SDK's `extra_headers=` keyword on `responses.stream(...)`, rather than passing it as a body field.

### Workaround

Until upstream lands a fix, I deployed a gateway:startup user hook that monkey-patches `ResponsesApiTransport.preflight_kwargs` to strip `extra_headers` from `api_kwargs` before serialization. Sharing here in case it's useful for others hitting this:

https://github.com/DmitryBMsk/hermes-agent-template/blob/main/hooks/codex-compat-patch/handler.py

With the workaround applied: primary `gpt-5.5/openai-codex` returns 200 in ~3s per call, no more fallback churn.

### Bonus finding (separate, downstream)

While probing, I also found two MCP tools (`mcp_gbrain_extract_facts`, `mcp_gbrain_log_ingest`) that fail Codex strict-mode JSON-schema validation with `Invalid schema for function 'X': array schema missing items` — but that's a `garrytan/gbrain` MCP server issue, not Hermes. Filed there separately.

### Bug Description

**Describe the bug**
The `hermes doctor` connectivity check (`_probe_apikey_provider`) falsely reports a valid Google Gemini API key (`GOOGLE_API_KEY`) as invalid with a red cross `✗ gemini (invalid API key)`. This happens because the health check treats the Gemini endpoint as OpenAI-compatible and uses the standard `Authorization: Bearer <key>` header, which Google AI Studio rejects with an HTTP 401 status code.

**To Reproduce**

1. Configure a valid `GOOGLE_API_KEY` in `~/.hermes/.env`.
2. Run `hermes doctor`.
3. See the `✗ gemini (invalid API key)` error in the API Connectivity section, even though the main `hermes` agent chat works perfectly fine with the exact same key.

**Root Cause Analysis**
In `/hermes_cli/doctor.py`, the generic helper function `_probe_apikey_provider` performs an HTTP GET request to check connectivity:

```python
headers = {
    "Authorization": f"Bearer {key}",
    "User-Agent": _HERMES_USER_AGENT,
}
r = httpx.get(url, headers=headers, timeout=10)

```

Google Gemini API does not authenticate via `Bearer` tokens in the standard `Authorization` header. It expects the API key either as a query parameter (`?key=...`) or via the `x-goog-api-key` header. Because `httpx` sends a `Bearer` token, Google returns `401 Unauthorized`, which the doctor script catches and flags as an `invalid API key` on line 1466:

```python
if r.status_code == 401:
    return _ConnectivityResult(
        pname,
        [(color("✗", Colors.RED), label, color("(invalid API key)", Colors.DIM))],
        [f"Check {env_vars[0]} in .env"],
    )

```

**Expected behavior**
The `_probe_apikey_provider` function should handle Gemini/Google specifically by using the correct authentication method (e.g., passing `x-goog-api-key` header or appending the key parameter to the URL) so that the health check passes successfully.

1. Configure a valid `GOOGLE_API_KEY` in `~/.hermes/.env`.
2. Run `hermes doctor` in the terminal.
3. Observe the `✗ gemini (invalid API key)` error in the "API Connectivity" section.

The `hermes doctor` command should successfully validate the Gemini API key and display a green checkmark `✓ gemini`, since the key is fully functional and the main `hermes` agent chat works perfectly with it.

items.title: gateway.pid and gateway.lock deleted after update restart, hiding send_message from CLI

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
## Summary

After `hermes update` (or the daily midnight auto-update) restarts the gateway, the files `gateway.pid` and `gateway.lock` are deleted from disk. The gateway process remains running, and the lock file is still held open (visible as `(deleted)` in `/proc/<pid>/fd/`), but the directory entries are gone.

## Impact

`is_gateway_running()` returns `False` because it checks for these files. The `send_message` tool is gated behind `_check_send_message()` which falls back to `is_gateway_running()` in CLI mode (platform = "local"). So `send_message` disappears from CLI sessions for ~24 hours after each midnight update, until the next manual `hermes gateway restart`.

## Root Cause

In `gateway/status.py`, `get_running_pid()` lines 938-940:

```python
lock_active = is_gateway_runtime_lock_active(resolved_lock_path)
if not lock_active:
    _cleanup_invalid_pid_path(resolved_pid_path, cleanup_stale=cleanup_stale)
    return None
```

When the lock file is missing from disk (e.g., deleted by a race in the `--replace` restart handoff), `is_gateway_runtime_lock_active()` returns `False` immediately. Then `_cleanup_invalid_pid_path()` force-unlinks both `gateway.pid` and `gateway.lock`. The PID file unlink is destructive — it may belong to a live gateway whose lock file was only deleted by the race.

The race: old gateway's `atexit` fires `remove_pid_file()` which unlinks `gateway.pid`. The new gateway starts via `--replace`, creates both files. But if the old process's atexit `release_gateway_runtime_lock()` closes the handle and something in the `--replace` flow calls `get_running_pid()` during the window when the lock file is absent, the PID file gets nuked.

## Suggested Fix

Only call `_cleanup_invalid_pid_path()` when the lock file actually exists on disk (meaning a dead process left it behind). When the lock file is simply missing, don't unlink the PID file — a live gateway may still own it:

```python
if not lock_active:
    if resolved_lock_path.exists():
        _cleanup_invalid_pid_path(resolved_pid_path, cleanup_stale=cleanup_stale)
    return None
```

The second call site (line 961, now 967) is reached when the lock IS active but records are invalid — that one should keep force-unlinking.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have gateway running with `send_message` tool visible in CLI
2. Run `hermes update` (or wait for midnight auto-update)
3. After restart, check: `ls ~/.hermes/gateway.pid ~/.hermes/gateway.lock` — both missing
4. `send_message` tool hidden from CLI sessions until manual `hermes gateway restart`

items.title: Gateway restart deadlocks on zombie-held scoped lock

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Problem

`acquire_scoped_lock()` in `gateway/status.py` uses `psutil.pid_exists()` to check whether a lock-holding PID is alive. This returns `True` for zombie (`<defunct>`) processes, so zombie-held locks are never cleaned up.

When a gateway process dies and leaves behind zombie children holding scoped locks (e.g., Telegram bot token locks), subsequent gateway restarts fail — the lock file appears valid and `--replace` is required to clear it manually.

## Root Cause

The stale-lock detection at line ~607 checks `/proc/<pid>/status` for the process state but only treats `T`/`t` (stopped/tracing stop) as stale. Zombies (`Z`/`z`) are not recognized.

## Fix

```diff
- if _state in {"T", "t"}:  # stopped or tracing stop
+ if _state in {"T", "t", "Z", "z"}:  # stopped, tracing stop, or zombie
```

## Repro

1. Start gateway with a Telegram bot
2. Gateway process dies abnormally, leaving zombie child holding the bot token lock
3. Attempt to restart gateway — it refuses, claiming lock is held by zombie PID

## Real-world occurrence

Observed on a production gateway (May 12, 2026): PID 2611 was a zombie from a previous gateway run. The lock file at `~/.local/state/hermes/gateway-locks/telegram-bot-token-*.lock` referenced this zombie PID, and `pid_exists()` returned `True`. The gateway refused to start until the lock was manually removed.

items.title: fix(curator): LLM consolidation pass uses skill_manage delete instead of terminal mv, bypassing .archive/ recovery

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
## Problem

The Curator's LLM consolidation pass instructs the agent to "archive" skills, but the LLM repeatedly uses `skill_manage(action='delete', absorbed_into='')` instead of `terminal` with `mv` to move the skill into `~/.hermes/skills/.archive/`.

This means "archived" skills are **permanently deleted** from the filesystem and are **not recoverable** via `hermes curator restore <name>`. They only survive in pre-run backups (tar.gz), and the `.archive/` directory is left empty even though the report claims skills were archived.

Additionally, the LLM pass has **no awareness of `archive_after_days: 90`** from the Curator config. It can archive (or delete) skills that are only days old, bypassing the configured timeout entirely.

This was observed with both **kimi-k2.6** and weaker models (e.g. gemini-2.5-flash-lite) on the Curator's consolidation pass.

## Root cause

The `CURATOR_REVIEW_PROMPT` (`agent/curator.py`, line 329+) tells the LLM:

- Rule 2: "DO NOT delete any skill. Archiving (moving to .archive/) is the maximum destructive action"
- But the LLM is given `skill_manage action=delete` as a valid tool and repeatedly uses it instead of `terminal mv`
- No mention of `archive_after_days` or `stale_after_days` in the prompt instructing the LLM to respect configured timeouts

## Expected behavior

1. LLM should only use `terminal` to `mv` skill directories into `.archive/`, never `skill_manage delete`
2. LLM should be instructed not to archive any skill younger than `archive_after_days` (configurable, default 90)
3. Optional: Config flag like `curator.llm_pass_enabled: false` to disable LLM pass while keeping auto-transitions

## Suggested fix

- Add `archive_after_days` and `stale_after_days` context to `CURATOR_REVIEW_PROMPT` with hard instruction not to touch younger skills
- Change tool instructions: only `terminal mv` for archiving, remove `skill_manage delete` from allowed tools during consolidation pass (or add a guard that intercepts delete and converts to mv)
- Consider adding `curator.llm_pass_enabled` config key

items.title: Discord adapter enters silent zombie state after network outage; never auto-reconnects

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
## Summary When the network drops out (VPN cycling, ISP blip, captive portal, etc.) and stays down for >60s, the Discord adapter can enter a "silent zombie" state: the process is alive, `_client` looks open, but the underlying socket is dead and **discord.py never triggers a reconnect**. The bot appears offline in Discord and only recovers via a full `hermes gateway restart`. This is reproducible across every profile on a host that uses an HTTP proxy that occasionally drops (in my case Shadowrocket on macOS). ## Repro / Symptoms In `~/.hermes/profiles/

/logs/gateway.log`, the last Discord-related lines are: ``` ERROR gateway.platforms.discord: ConnectionTimeoutError: Connection timeout to host https://discord.com/api/v10/channels/.../messages ERROR gateway.platforms.base: [Discord] Fallback send also failed: ... ``` …and then **nothing**. No `Disconnected`, no `Reconnect`, no `Connected as`. The process keeps running, cron fires, other adapters work — but Discord is dead until manual restart. Process can sit in this state for 13+ hours. In my case 6 profile gateways got stuck simultaneously after a brief proxy outage; only the main profile (which happened to receive a new inbound message that hit the WS layer) self-healed. ## Root cause (suspected) `gateway/platforms/discord.py` calls `self._client.start(self.config.token)` once in `connect()` (line ~849). discord.py's built-in reconnect handles WebSocket drops, but a REST timeout in the message-send path doesn't notify the gateway WS layer, so when the WS itself silently dies (TCP RST not delivered through a dead proxy) there's no signal to rebuild the client. Compare to discord.js (Node), which couples shard health to REST failure rate and self-heals through the same scenario indefinitely without external intervention. ## Proposed fix Add a periodic liveness probe in `DiscordAdapter.connect()`: ```python async def _liveness_loop(): fails = 0 while self._running: await asyncio.sleep(60) try: # Cheap REST call that exercises the same path as message send await self._client.fetch_user(self._client.user.id) fails = 0 except Exception as e: fails += 1 logger.warning("[%s] Discord liveness probe failed (%d/3): %s", self.name, fails, e) if fails >= 3: logger.error("[%s] Discord client appears dead, forcing reconnect", self.name) try: await self._client.close() # outer start() loop will reconnect except Exception: pass fails = 0 self._liveness_task = asyncio.create_task(_liveness_loop()) ``` Cancel the task in `disconnect()`. Tunable interval/threshold via config (`discord.liveness_interval`, `discord.liveness_failure_threshold`). Alternative: hook into the existing send-failure path in `gateway/platforms/base.py` and trigger `client.close()` after N consecutive REST timeouts to the Discord API. Cleaner signal but touches two files. ## Workaround External watchdog cron that polls `https://discord.com/api/v10/gateway` through both proxy and direct, and `hermes --profile

gateway restart`s any profile whose log shows an unrecovered error >5min old. Works but feels like papering over a fixable bug. ## Environment - macOS 26.5 - Hermes commit: `942adf617` - discord.py: - Proxy: Shadowrocket HTTP @ 127.0.0.1:1082

items.title: [feishu] Remove markdown table force-text workaround — Feishu now supports tables in post format
items.body:
## Summary

In `gateway/platforms/feishu.py`, `_build_outbound_payload` has a workaround that detects markdown tables and forces them to `msg_type=text` instead of allowing them through the normal post rendering pipeline:

```python
_MARKDOWN_TABLE_RE = re.compile(r"^\|.*\|\n\|[-|: ]+\|", re.MULTILINE)
# ...
if _MARKDOWN_TABLE_RE.search(content):
    text_payload = {"text": content}
    return "text", json.dumps(text_payload, ensure_ascii=False)
```

## Problem

This was a workaround for older Feishu/Lark SDK versions where post-type `md` elements rendered markdown tables as blank. **This is no longer an issue** — Feishu now correctly renders tables in post format.

The workaround causes table-heavy messages (common in financial dashboards, data reports, etc.) to lose all formatting and display as raw plain text on the client, which is worse than the original problem.

## Proposed fix

Remove `_MARKDOWN_TABLE_RE` and the corresponding `if` branch in `_build_outbound_payload`, letting table content flow through the normal post rendering pipeline.

## Impact

Only affects the Feishu/Lark platform adapter. The change is safe because:
- Feishu now natively supports table rendering in post format
- Non-table messages are unaffected
- The `_MARKDOWN_HINT_RE` check (which covers all other markdown formatting) remains in place

---

I have been running this patch locally for a while with no issues. Happy to open a PR if preferred.

items.title: fix(update): hermes update on Windows fails to quarantine hermes.exe when another instance is running

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
## Summary

`hermes update` on Windows fails to replace `hermes.exe` because the running process holds the file open, and the existing `.exe.old.<ts>` quarantine workaround in `_quarantine_running_hermes_exe()` doesn't always succeed. The git-pull update path then bails out with exit code 2 from `uv pip install -e .` and the ZIP fallback path takes over. ZIP fallback works, so the update technically completes, but:

- The user sees scary `[WinError 32] The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process` warnings.
- The git-pull fast path (preferred) is silently abandoned.
- The fallback runs again, hits the *same* failure, and emits the same warning a second time before it succeeds.

The `_quarantine_running_hermes_exe()` helper exists specifically to handle this on Windows (rename `hermes.exe` -> `hermes.exe.old.<unix-ms>` so `uv` can write a fresh shim at the original path). It works for plain `hermes update` from a terminal, but not when the Hermes Desktop Electron app is running, because the desktop has its own spawned `hermes.EXE` child process keeping the file open.

## Evidence

From a user log (`~/.hermes/logs/update.log`):

```
=== hermes update started 2026-05-12T15:17:27 ===
- Updating Hermes Agent...

-> Fetching updates...
-> Found 2 new commit(s)
  Pre-update snapshot: 20260512-221728-pre-update
-> Pulling updates...
  Cleared 51 stale __pycache__ directories
-> Updating Python dependencies...
  WARN: Could not quarantine hermes.exe: [WinError 32] The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process: 'C:\Users\NVIDIA\AppData\Local\hermes\hermes-agent\venv\Scripts\hermes.exe' -> 'C:\Users\NVIDIA\AppData\Local\hermes\hermes-agent\venv\Scripts\hermes.exe.old.1778624248702'
  WARN: Optional extras failed, reinstalling base dependencies and retrying extras individually...
  WARN: Could not quarantine hermes.exe: [WinError 32] ... hermes.exe.old.1778624250832'
WARN: Git update failed: Command '['C:\Users\NVIDIA\.local\bin\uv.EXE', 'pip', 'install', '-e', '.']' returned non-zero exit status 2.
-> Falling back to ZIP download...

-> Downloading latest version...
-> Extracting...
Updated 84 items from ZIP
-> Updating Python dependencies...
  WARN: Could not quarantine hermes.exe: [WinError 32] ... hermes.exe.old.1778624278715'
  WARN: Optional extras failed, reinstalling base dependencies and retrying extras individually...
  WARN: Could not quarantine hermes.exe: [WinError 32] ... hermes.exe.old.1778624280560'
```

Four `WinError 32` warnings in one update. The user successfully ended up on the new version (via ZIP), but the experience is broken.

Context: this user was running the Hermes Desktop Electron app (PR #20059, branch `bb/gui`). The desktop spawns the backend via `hermes.EXE`, so during update there are at least two `hermes.exe` instances alive (the user-invoked update process and the desktop-spawned backend).

## Root cause

`_quarantine_running_hermes_exe()` in `hermes_cli/main.py` (~L6940) tries `Path.rename()` on `hermes.exe`. On Windows, renaming a running .exe usually works because Windows tracks the file by handle, not path -- but it fails when:

1. **Another process has the file open with FILE_SHARE_DELETE cleared.** This is what `[WinError 32]` means. Some AV products and Defender real-time scanners hold transient handles without the share-delete flag while scanning.

2. **The desktop wrapper has spawned `hermes.EXE` as a child.** The child process locks the parent .exe inode independently of the user-invoked `hermes update` process.

3. **A second `hermes.exe` invocation overlapped the update window** -- e.g. the user double-clicked the desktop icon, or a previous gateway/cron worker is still alive.

Currently the code catches `OSError`, logs `Could not quarantine`, and continues -- relying on `uv` to overwrite the file in place. `uv pip install -e .` *can* overwrite a loaded .exe on some Windows configurations, but not all, and when it fails it exits 2 with no useful diagnostic.

## Proposed fixes (in order of preference)

### 1. Detect concurrent `hermes.exe` processes and refuse to update

If another `hermes.exe` is alive (including the desktop's child process), `hermes update` should print a clear message and abort before doing anything destructive:

```
hermes update detected another hermes.exe is running:
  PID 12345  C:\Users\NVIDIA\...\hermes.exe  (Hermes Desktop backend)

Close Hermes Desktop (or stop the gateway with `hermes gateway stop`)
before updating. The update will not proceed while another instance is
holding the executable open.
```

Implementation: enumerate processes with `psutil.process_iter(['exe', 'pid'])` (already a Hermes dep), match on `exe` ending in the active venv's `hermes.exe`, exclude the current PID. If any match, print and exit non-zero.

### 2. Use `MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING | MOVEFILE_DELAY_UNTIL_REBOOT` for stubborn cases

When the rename fails, fall back to `MoveFileEx` with `MOVEFILE_DELAY_UNTIL_REBOOT`. This schedules the replacement for the next reboot via `PendingFileRenameOperations`, so the running .exe is left alone until a reboot. We can prefer this over ZIP fallback when the git-pull is otherwise successful -- the `_quarantine_running_hermes_exe` block is the ONLY thing that fails.

### 3. Retry the rename with exponential backoff

The AV-handle-during-scan case is transient (typically <1s). Try 3-5 times with 100/250/500/1000ms sleeps before giving up. Cheap, catches the common case.

### 4. Improve the warning message

Even if (1)-(3) aren't implemented, the warning should at least say *what to do*:

```
WARN: Could not quarantine hermes.exe (another process is holding it open).
   Close Hermes Desktop / stop the gateway / disable AV temporarily, then re-run.
```

Right now the warning is hostile -- a `WinError 32` and a Windows path with no remediation hint.

### 5. Skip rename if uv can overwrite anyway

The whole quarantine dance only matters when `uv pip install -e .` would otherwise fail with `Access is denied. (os error 5)`. Try uv first, *then* fall back to quarantine + retry only on access-denied. This avoids touching the .exe at all in the common case where the update is run from a terminal with no other instances alive.

## Reproduction

1. Install Hermes on Windows via the standard installer.
2. Launch Hermes Desktop (PR #20059's `bb/gui` branch, or any context that keeps `hermes.exe` alive).
3. From a separate terminal: `hermes update`.
4. Observe `[WinError 32]` warning in `update.log` and `uv pip install -e .` exit 2.
5. ZIP fallback completes successfully and user reaches the new version.

## Severity

P3 -- update succeeds via the ZIP fallback path, so no user is *blocked*. But:
- Update takes 2-3x longer than necessary (ZIP download + extract + reinstall vs git pull + uv install).
- Scary warnings undermine confidence in the update system.
- The fallback also fails to quarantine, so the failure is replicated downstream.

## Relevant files

- `hermes_cli/main.py` -- `_quarantine_running_hermes_exe()` (~L6940), `_restore_quarantined_exes()` (~L6973), `_cleanup_quarantined_exes()` (~L6983), update entry points around the `update` CLI command.
- `apps/desktop/electron/main.cjs` (PR #20059) -- backend spawn logic that creates the concurrent `hermes.EXE` instance.

## Related

- PR #26618 (just merged) fixed two unrelated Windows log-spam bugs surfaced from the same user log capture.
- PR #20059 (`bb/gui`) ships the Hermes Desktop app whose backend-spawn pattern triggers this issue when running.

### Bug Description

I ran into a misleading 'hermes doctor' case with OAuth-backed providers.

In my setup, Hermes was using Nous Portal, and Google Gemini OAuth was already logged in and healthy. But `hermes doctor` still surfaced 'Check GOOGLE_API_KEY in .env' in the final summary because the direct Gemini API key probe failed.

The same logic also applies to provider families like MiniMax, where a healthy OAuth path can coexist with a bad direct API key.

That feels wrong because the API Connectivity section can still show the bad key, but the final summary should be reserved for blocking issues. If the OAuth path for that provider family is already healthy, the direct-key failure is no longer a blocking setup problem.

Expected behavior:
- keep the 'invalid API key' line in API Connectivity
- do not promote it into the final blocking summary when a healthy OAuth fallback already exists


### Steps to Reproduce

1. Log into `Google Gemini OAuth` so the OAuth path is healthy.
2. Leave an invalid `GOOGLE_API_KEY` configured in `~/.hermes/.env`.
3. Run `hermes doctor`.
4. Check the API Connectivity section.
5. Check the final issues summary.
6. Notice that doctor still reports `Check GOOGLE_API_KEY in .env` as a blocking summary issue even though the Gemini OAuth path is already healthy.


### Expected Behavior

The API Connectivity section can still report that the direct API key is invalid.

But if the matching OAuth path is already healthy, that direct-key problem should not be promoted into the final blocking summary.


### Actual Behavior

`hermes doctor` still promotes the bad direct API key into the final summary, even when the matching OAuth path is already healthy.

In my repro, Hermes was using a healthy OAuth-backed setup, but doctor still ended with:

`Check GOOGLE_API_KEY in .env`

That makes the setup look more broken than it really is.


### Affected Component

CLI (interactive chat)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

_No response_

### Debug Report

```shell
Report     https://paste.rs/Sw0iF
agent.log  https://paste.rs/0FCf8
```

### Operating System

Ubuntu on WSL2 (Windows 11)

### Python Version

Python 3.12.3

### Hermes Version

Hermes Agent v0.13.0 (2026.5.7)

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell
A representative real-world symptom was:

- healthy 'Google Gemini OAuth' shown in the Auth Providers section
- but 'Check GOOGLE_API_KEY in .env' still appeared in the final summary

The API Connectivity section can correctly show an invalid direct key, but the final blocking summary should not treat it as a setup blocker when the OAuth path is already healthy.
```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

I traced this to the API Connectivity summary handling in `hermes_cli/doctor.py`.

Each connectivity probe returns both display lines and summary issues. Later in `run_doctor`, those issues are appended directly into the final summary.

That means a failed direct API-key probe can become a final blocking issue even when the same provider family already has a healthy OAuth runtime path.

I prepared a fix that keeps the failed connectivity row visible, but suppresses the final summary issue when a healthy OAuth fallback already exists for the same provider family.

- `hermes_cli/doctor.py`


### Proposed Fix (optional)

Keep the failed API Connectivity row visible, but do not promote the direct-key issue into the final blocking summary when the same provider family already has a healthy OAuth fallback.
I also added focused regression coverage for:
- Gemini OAuth + invalid direct Gemini key
- MiniMax OAuth + invalid direct MiniMax key

items.body:
### Problem or Use Case

Hermes Agent adoption is accelerating rapidly, and users often employ it to orchestrate the activity of a multitude of other AI agents. Today, we already have basic analytics in Hermes Dashboard but there is **no consolidated visibility across multiple agents**: token usage, model costs, reasoning traces, and tool-call patterns across sessions. 

[TokenTelemetry](https://tokentelemetry.com/) is open source and offers just that with one command — **no signup, no cloud, nothing leaves your machine** — local, read-only observability for Claude Code, Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, Copilot, Antigravity, OpenCode.

### Proposed Solution

Develop of a **Hermes plugin** that integrates with **TokenTelemetry** project to expose a unified multi-agent telemetry panel inside the Hermes Dashboard.

TokenTelemetry is:
- designed to unify logs from multiple agents into a single view
- agent‑log–driven, i.e. no SDK or instrumentation
- 100% local operation with self‑hosted dashboard
- written in Python & TypeScript (like Hermes itself)
- open source with MIT license (star their [repo](https://github.com/VasiHemanth/tokentelemetry/))

### Additional Context
The TokenTelemetry project is very young (less than a month old) and **does NOT yet support Hermes Agent**. It is, however, fairly straighfoward to implement by reading the `~/.hermes/state.db` following the pattern of their existing parser for OpenCode (also based on a SQLite database); in fact, it's even simpler because Hermes Agent already has token counts pre‑aggregated per session (in the `sessions` table). See feature request in their repo: (https://github.com/VasiHemanth/tokentelemetry/issues/20)

Raising awareness here to attract contributors interested in building a Hermes plugin and/or a parser to enable support in TokenTelemetry. Happy to pick it up if there is sufficient interest from this community (**NB:** however I'm not much of a front-end dev, so Hermes & Co would have to do most of the heavy-lifting ;-)

### Alternatives Considered

- External dashboards (Langfuse, Helicone, LangSmith) → Require cloud accounts or instrumentation; not aligned with Hermes’ local‑first philosophy.  
 
- Manual log inspection or scripted analytics → Not scalable or user‑friendly. Reinventing the wheel.
 
- Here, I also found issue #6642 but the scope doesn't seem to include multiple agents, even if lays the groundwork for it... Nonetheless, that one looks like a much more ambitious effort than my proposal above.

items.body:
## Symptom

Quoting `enabled: "false"` (YAML string) under any `platforms.<name>` entry in `config.yaml` leaves the platform **enabled** instead of disabling it. Bare `enabled: false` (YAML bool) works correctly.

## Reproduction

`tests/gateway/test_config.py::TestLoadGatewayConfig::test_bridges_quoted_false_platform_enabled_from_config_yaml` fails on the current main branch:

```
config.yaml:
  platforms:
    api_server:
      enabled: "false"

assert config.platforms[Platform.API_SERVER].enabled is False
E   AssertionError: assert True is False
E    +  where True = PlatformConfig(enabled=True, ...).enabled
```

## Likely root cause

`gateway/config.py:857` does a raw passthrough:

```python
if enabled_was_explicit:
    plat_data["enabled"] = platform_cfg["enabled"]
```

Whatever YAML loads — `"false"` (str), `False` (bool), or `0` (int) — is forwarded unchanged. Downstream, the non-empty string `"false"` is truthy, so the platform stays enabled.

Other call sites that build `enabled` (e.g. lines 326, 388) correctly route through `_coerce_bool()`. This passthrough path doesn't.

## Suggested fix

Apply `_coerce_bool()` at line 857 (or in `PlatformConfig.__post_init__` for defence in depth):

```python
plat_data["enabled"] = _coerce_bool(platform_cfg["enabled"], False)
```

## Impact

P2 — silent footgun for anyone editing `config.yaml` by hand and quoting booleans (e.g., users coming from Docker/K8s envs where everything is a string). Disabled-on-paper platforms silently start receiving traffic.

## Environment

- Discovered against current `~/.hermes/hermes-agent` checkout, Python 3.11.15
- Pytest 23076 tests passed / 2 failed / 59 skipped — this is one of the two failures

items.body:
# Kanban Worker Context Pollution Bug Report

## Summary

Kanban workers fail to execute tasks due to context pollution from the dispatcher's session. Workers inherit the full conversation history of the parent session, causing them to ignore the task and exit prematurely without calling any kanban tools.

## Priority

**High** - This is a bug fix (Priority #1 in CONTRIBUTING.md). Kanban is currently unusable for task execution.

## Environment

- **Hermes Version**: Latest (as of 2026-05-16)
- **Platform**: Linux (Ubuntu)
- **Python**: 3.x
- **Model**: Claude Sonnet 4.5 (via custom provider)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start a Hermes session with some conversation history (e.g., discussing recipes, Obsidian, etc.)
2. Create a simple Kanban task:
   ```bash
   hermes kanban create "测试任务：统计家常菜菜单里有多少道菜，按分类列出数量" --assignee default
   ```
3. Dispatch the task:
   ```bash
   hermes kanban dispatch --max 1
   ```
4. Check the task status:
   ```bash
   hermes kanban show <task_id>
   ```

## Expected Behavior

The worker should:
1. Call `kanban_show()` to orient itself (per KANBAN_GUIDANCE step 1)
2. Read the菜单 file
3. Count dishes by category
4. Call `kanban_complete()` with results

## Actual Behavior

The worker:
1. Says "我来查看任务详情" (I'll check the task details)
2. **Does not call any tools** (no `kanban_show()`, no `read_file()`, nothing)
3. Exits immediately (duration: 4-5 seconds)
4. Crashes with "pid not alive"
5. Retries once, crashes again
6. Gets auto-blocked after 2 consecutive crashes

## Root Cause Analysis

### Code Location

`hermes_cli/kanban_db.py`, lines 3931-4006:

```python
prompt = f"work kanban task {task.id}"
# ...
cmd = [
    *_resolve_hermes_argv(),
    "-p", profile_arg,
    "--skills", "kanban-worker",
    # ... per-task skills ...
    "chat",
    "-q", prompt,  # ← THE PROBLEM
]
```

### The Problem

1. **Worker uses `chat` command**: The dispatcher spawns workers with `hermes chat -q "work kanban task <id>"`
2. **Context inheritance**: The `chat` command inherits the **full conversation history** from the dispatcher's session
3. **Context pollution**: When the dispatcher is running inside an active Hermes session (e.g., via Gateway/Telegram), the worker sees:
   - All previous user messages
   - All previous assistant responses
   - Context compaction summaries
   - Unrelated work (菜谱, Obsidian, etc.)
4. **Agent confusion**: The worker agent sees this massive context, gets confused, and:
   - Responds with a vague acknowledgment ("我来查看任务详情")
   - **Never calls any tools**
   - Exits without completing the lifecycle

### Evidence

From `hermes kanban log <task_id>`:

```
Query: work kanban task t_7e404f63
Initializing agent...
────────────────────────────────────────

╭─ ⚕ Hermes ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
    我来查看任务详情。
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯

Session:        20260516_113400_a0b7fa
Duration:       5s
Messages:       2 (1 user, 0 tool calls)  ← NO TOOL CALLS!
```

The session export shows the worker received:
- The task prompt: `"work kanban task t_7e404f63"`
- **Plus** context compaction summaries from the parent session
- **Plus** unrelated conversation history (菜谱, Obsidian, daily reports, etc.)

## Impact

- **Kanban is completely broken** for task execution
- Workers crash 100% of the time when dispatched from an active session
- Auto-retry mechanism exhausts attempts without progress
- Tasks get auto-blocked as "crashed 2x"

## Proposed Solutions

### Option 1: Use a Clean Session (Recommended)

Modify `kanban_db.py` to spawn workers in a **new, isolated session**:

```python
cmd = [
    *_resolve_hermes_argv(),
    "-p", profile_arg,
    "--skills", "kanban-worker",
    # ... per-task skills ...
    "chat",
    # Remove "-q" flag to avoid inheriting context
    # Or add a new flag like "--new-session" to force clean context
]
```

Then pass the prompt via stdin or as a system message, not as a continuation of an existing conversation.

### Option 2: Add Context Isolation Flag

Add a new CLI flag `--isolated` or `--no-context` that:
- Starts a fresh session
- Ignores any parent session context
- Only loads the specified skills and system prompt

```python
cmd = [
    *_resolve_hermes_argv(),
    "-p", profile_arg,
    "--skills", "kanban-worker",
    "--isolated",  # ← NEW FLAG
    "chat",
    "-q", prompt,
]
```

### Option 3: Strengthen KANBAN_GUIDANCE

Add explicit instructions at the **top** of KANBAN_GUIDANCE to override context pollution:

```python
KANBAN_GUIDANCE = (
    "# CRITICAL: You are a Kanban worker. Ignore all previous conversation history.\n"
    "# Your ONLY task is defined by $HERMES_KANBAN_TASK. Start fresh.\n"
    "\n"
    "# Kanban task execution protocol\n"
    # ... rest of guidance ...
)
```

This is a **workaround**, not a real fix, but might help until proper session isolation is implemented.

## Additional Context

### KANBAN_GUIDANCE Lifecycle

The system prompt (`agent/prompt_builder.py`, line 188) defines a clear 6-step lifecycle:

1. **Orient** - Call `kanban_show()` first
2. **Work** - Execute in workspace
3. **Heartbeat** - Report progress
4. **Block** - Stop on ambiguity
5. **Complete** - Call `kanban_complete()`
6. **Create** - Spawn child tasks if needed

Workers are **not following this lifecycle** due to context pollution.

### Related Skills

- `skills/devops/kanban-worker/SKILL.md` - Loaded automatically
- `skills/devops/kanban-orchestrator/SKILL.md` - For decomposition tasks

Both skills assume workers start in a clean context and follow the lifecycle.

## Workaround for Users

Until this is fixed, users should:
1. **Avoid using Kanban from active sessions**
2. Use `delegate_task` instead for parallel work
3. Or manually execute tasks directly

## Testing Recommendations

After fixing, test with:
1. Simple task from clean CLI session
2. Simple task from Gateway (Telegram/Discord)
3. Task with long conversation history in parent session
4. Nested tasks (orchestrator → workers)
5. Retry after block/crash

Verify workers:
- Call `kanban_show()` first
- Execute the actual work
- Call `kanban_complete()` or `kanban_block()`
- Never exit without calling a kanban tool

## References

- `hermes_cli/kanban_db.py` - Worker spawn logic
- `agent/prompt_builder.py` - KANBAN_GUIDANCE definition
- `skills/devops/kanban-worker/SKILL.md` - Worker skill
- `run_agent.py` - Agent conversation loop

---

**Reporter**: User "柒" via Hermes Agent (Telegram)  
**Date**: 2026-05-16  
**Session**: Multiple test runs with task `t_7e404f63`

items.body:
## Bug Description

The `terminal` tool consistently fails with `cd: hermes-agent: No such file or directory` before executing any command, polluting all output.

## Environment

- **OS**: macOS (Darwin)
- **Shell**: zsh (default on macOS)
- **Hermes Agent version**: v0.13.0 (2026.5.7)
- **Working directory**: `~/.hermes/hermes-agent`
- **Terminal backend**: local

## Reproduction

Any `terminal` tool invocation produces the error:

```
$ echo "test"
/opt/homebrew/bin/bash: line 2: cd: hermes-agent: No such file or directory
```

Even simple commands like `echo test123` or `pwd` fail with the same error.

## Root Cause Analysis

The terminal tool's wrapper automatically prepends `cd hermes-agent` before executing commands. However:

1. The current working directory is already `~/.hermes/hermes-agent`
2. The `cd` command uses a **relative path** (`hermes-agent`)
3. This resolves to `~/.hermes/hermes-agent/hermes-agent` which does not exist
4. The error appears even though the actual command still executes

## Verification

- **Shell configs are clean**: Checked `~/.bashrc`, `~/.bash_profile`, `~/.profile`, `~/.zshrc`, `~/.zprofile` — none contain `cd hermes-agent`
- **Other tools work fine**: `execute_code` and `browser_navigate` are unaffected
- **Network access works**: Confirmed via `execute_code` with `urllib.request`

## Expected Behavior

The terminal tool should either:
1. Use an absolute path: `cd ~/.hermes/hermes-agent`
2. Check if already in the target directory before cd
3. Or not prepend `cd` at all if already in the correct directory

## Workaround

Use `execute_code` (Python) or `browser_navigate` instead of `terminal` for now.

## Additional Context

This appears to be a regression or oversight in the terminal backend wrapper, where the `cd` prefix doesn't account for the case where the CWD is already the target directory.

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## Problem

When the auxiliary LLM provider (used for context compression, memory flush, web extraction, etc.) returns a 429 rate limit with a daily quota message like `"Too many tokens per day"`, the fallback chain in `call_llm()` does not activate. This causes context compaction to silently fail, dropping conversation history without a summary.

Two root causes:

### 1. Daily rate limits not classified as fallback-worthy errors

`_is_payment_error()` checks for keywords like "credits", "insufficient funds", "billing", "payment required" — but daily token quota exhaustion (common with Bedrock, Vertex AI, and other cloud providers) uses different language like "Too many tokens per day" or "quota exceeded". These are functionally identical to credit exhaustion but don't trigger fallback.

**Suggested fix:** Add quota-related keywords to `_is_payment_error()` or create a separate `_is_quota_error()`:
```python
# In _is_payment_error or a new _is_quota_exhaustion check:
if any(kw in err_lower for kw in ("quota", "too many tokens", "rate limit exceeded",
                                    "daily limit", "tokens per day")):
    return True
```

### 2. Fallback chain gated on `resolved_provider == "auto"` only

In `call_llm()` (~line 2293):
```python
is_auto = resolved_provider in ("auto", "", None)
if should_fallback and is_auto:
```

When a task resolves to a specific provider (e.g., "custom" for a LiteLLM proxy, or "openrouter"), the fallback chain is completely disabled. If that provider fails with a retriable error, `call_llm` raises instead of trying alternatives.

This is overly conservative. The intent is to respect explicit provider choice, but when the error is clearly "this provider can't serve right now" (payment, quota, connection), trying alternatives is better than failing entirely — especially for background tasks like context compression where the user didn't explicitly choose a provider.

**Suggested fix:** Allow fallback for quota/payment/connection errors regardless of provider resolution source, or at minimum for tasks where the provider was resolved via auto-detection chain rather than explicit user config:
```python
# Allow fallback when the error is clearly about provider capacity,
# not about the request itself (4xx client errors etc.)
if should_fallback:
    # ... try fallback chain
```

## Impact

- Context compaction fails silently when the primary provider hits daily limits
- Middle conversation turns are dropped without summary
- Agent loses task context and starts repeating work or acting confused
- Affects any deployment using provider rate limits (Bedrock, Vertex AI, free-tier OpenRouter, etc.)

## Environment

- hermes-agent 0.8.0
- LiteLLM proxy routing to Bedrock (daily token limit) with Anthropic as fallback
- Context compressor calls `call_llm(task="compression", ...)` which resolves to the custom/litellm provider

items.body:
# Bug Report: `.env` File Silently Stripped During `hermes update` / Config Migration

## Summary

Running `hermes update` or `hermes config migrate` silently strips user-added environment variables from `~/.hermes/.env`, removing all custom sections (Telegram, DeepSeek, browser settings, terminal overrides, debug flags) and replacing them with a fresh template. Only "standard" sections recognized by the internal template survive. This causes silent loss of critical API keys and platform credentials.

**Severity: HIGH** — Causes complete loss of messaging platform connectivity (Telegram, Discord, etc.) and API access (search, web extraction, custom providers) until the user manually restores keys from a pre-update snapshot.

## Environment

- **Hermes commit**: `9fb40e6a3` (May 15, 2026)
- **OS**: Linux 6.8.0-31-generic (Ubuntu)
- **Python**: 3.11
- **Install method**: Git clone
- **Profiles**: Single (default)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start with a working `.env` containing custom sections (e.g., Telegram bot token, DeepSeek API key, browser settings, terminal overrides, debug flags)
2. Run `hermes update` (which triggers config migration)
3. OR run `hermes config migrate` directly
4. Compare `.env` before and after

## Expected Behavior

`.env` should be **preserved in full** — existing keys should never be removed. Migration should only **add** new missing keys (commented out by default), never delete user-set values.

## Actual Behavior

`.env` is silently rewritten from an internal template, dropping all unrecognized sections. Output:

```
=== .env Before (May 14 snapshot) ===
473 lines — contains Telegram, DeepSeek, browser, terminal, debug config

=== .env After (May 15 post-update) ===
212 lines — 261 lines GONE (55% of file)

=== What Was Lost ===
BROWSERBASE_ADVANCED_STEALTH
BROWSERBASE_PROXIES
BROWSER_INACTIVITY_TIMEOUT
BROWSER_SESSION_TIMEOUT
DEEPSEEK_API_KEY
IMAGE_TOOLS_DEBUG
MOA_TOOLS_DEBUG
TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USERS
TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN
TELEGRAM_HOME_CHANNEL
TERMINAL_LIFETIME_SECONDS
TERMINAL_MODAL_IMAGE
TERMINAL_TIMEOUT
VISION_TOOLS_DEBUG
WEB_TOOLS_DEBUG
```

## Impact

- **All messaging platforms go offline** — missing `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` causes gateway to start with "No messaging platforms enabled"
- **Primary API key lost** — `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` dropped, LLM calls fail
- **Web search breaks** — TAVILY_API_KEY, FIRECRAWL_API_KEY stripped
- **All cron deliveries silently fail** — jobs run but can't deliver to Telegram
- **User must manually restore keys from pre-update snapshot** (`~/.hermes/state-snapshots/`)

## Workaround

The pre-update snapshot mechanism (`~/.hermes/state-snapshots/<timestamp>-pre-update/.env`) preserves the original `.env`, allowing manual recovery. Users should verify `.env` integrity after every update:

```bash
diff ~/.hermes/.env ~/.hermes/state-snapshots/$(ls -t ~/.hermes/state-snapshots/ | head -1)/.env
```

## Suspected Root Cause

The config migration/sanitization flow (`hermes_cli/config.py` — `sanitize_env_file()`, `_write_env_vars()`, and related functions) regenerates `.env` from a template of known keys. Keys not in the `OPTIONAL_ENV_VARS` + `_EXTRA_ENV_KEYS` known-keys set are silently dropped.

Additionally, `_sanitize_env_lines()` (line 4400) uses `known_keys = set(OPTIONAL_ENV_VARS.keys()) | _EXTRA_ENV_KEYS` — any key NOT in this set may be treated as a concatenation artifact and split/dropped.

## Related

- This appears related to the known issue where "hermes update temporarily blanks API keys during restart" (documented in community discussions)
- Similar reports may exist for config loss during `hermes setup` wizard runs

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
## Bug

When the gateway's busy-input mode is `steer` (or `queue`), sending `/stop` or `/interrupt` to an actively running agent from a gateway platform (Slack, Telegram, Discord, etc.) does **not** interrupt the agent. Instead, the slash command text is fed into `running_agent.steer()` and the agent receives `/stop` as a mid-turn user instruction — which it just incorporates as more context.

## Repro

1. Set gateway `busy_input_mode: steer` (the recommended default for active-conversation platforms).
2. From Slack/Telegram/Discord, send a prompt that triggers a long-running turn (lots of tool calls).
3. Mid-turn, send `/stop` (or `!stop` on Slack via the bang-rewrite path, since native slashes don't fire in Slack threads).
4. Observe: agent keeps running. `agent.log` shows e.g.:
   ```
   Delivered /steer to agent after tool batch (N chars): /stop
   ```

## Expected

`/stop` and `/interrupt` should always interrupt the running agent, regardless of `busy_input_mode`. They're control commands, not user input.

## Root cause

`gateway/run.py::_handle_active_session_busy_message` reads `effective_mode = self._busy_input_mode` and then branches into steer/queue/interrupt **without first checking whether `event.text` is one of the known gateway control commands**. So in steer mode, `/stop` text gets passed to `running_agent.steer("/stop")` and the agent treats it as text.

## Suggested fix

Before the steer/queue branching block, parse the first token of `event.text`. If it resolves to `stop` or `interrupt` (using the existing `is_gateway_known_command` helper or a small allowlist), override `effective_mode = "interrupt"` so the existing interrupt branch fires.

Sketch:

```python
effective_mode = self._busy_input_mode
_text = (event.text or "").lstrip()
if _text.startswith("/"):
    first = _text.split(maxsplit=1)[0][1:].split("@", 1)[0].lower()
    if first in ("stop", "interrupt"):
        effective_mode = "interrupt"
```

(Locally patched in `gateway/run.py` ~line 2547. Happy to send a PR — opening this issue first to confirm direction.)

## Why this hurts on Slack specifically

Slack blocks native slash commands inside threads. The existing `!cmd` rewrite path (`gateway/platforms/slack.py` ~line 1814) gracefully converts `!stop` → `/stop`, so users in threads already have a working command path — except this bug means it doesn't actually stop the agent. End result: from a Slack thread, there is *no* working way to interrupt an in-flight agent, since both native `/stop` and `!stop` get steered as text.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent installed via `hermes update` workflow
- macOS 26.4.1
- Default `busy_input_mode: steer` (configured)
- Slack gateway in Socket Mode

## WeChat rate-limit retry storm causes gateway OOM and eventual SIGKILL (no circuit breaker)

### Description

When iLink/WeChat enters a persistent rate-limiting state (errcode -2), the `_send_text_chunk` retry loop in `gateway/platforms/weixin.py` retries each individual chunk with backoff, but there is **no circuit breaker across invocations**. When the agent has multiple messages queued (e.g. long multi-part replies, tool results, or cron-initiated push messages arriving during a rate-limit window), every message spawns its own retry loop. These stack up concurrently, creating a retry storm.

### Observed behavior

- Multiple WARNING logs: `[Weixin] rate limited for <user>; backing off 3.0s before retry`
- After 30+ retries across many messages in ~30 seconds, gateway memory spikes to **3.4GB**
- Gateway becomes unresponsive, eventually hits systemd's 90s timeout
- systemd sends SIGTERM → gateway can't drain in time → SIGKILL

### Relevant code

`gateway/platforms/weixin.py` lines 1622–1643 — per-chunk rate-limit backoff loop, but with no cross-invocation throttling or circuit breaker.

### Expected behavior

After N consecutive rate-limit rejections within a time window, the gateway should **stop retrying and raise the error** (at least for that platform, ideally for that specific chat/account). A circuit breaker pattern:

1. Increment a counter on each rate-limit event (per chat or global)
2. When counter exceeds threshold in a time window, stop all pending sends and surface the error
3. Reset the breaker after a cooldown period (e.g. 30-60s without a rate limit)

### Environment

- Hermes commit: latest main as of 2026-05-16
- Platform: WeChat (iLink)
- The retry logic exists but lacks cross-invocation throttling
- Related: #21011, #21061 (cover rate limiting but not the retry storm OOM failure mode)

### Sample logs

```
May 16 07:35:13 WARNING [Weixin] rate limited for o9cq800p; backing off 3.0s
May 16 07:35:16 WARNING [Weixin] rate limited for o9cq800p; backing off 3.0s
... (30+ times) ...
```

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
### Problem or Use Case

I need to schedule tasks (e.g., daily briefing, weekly plan) that only run on actual workdays, respecting China's complex holiday and compensatory workday rules (e.g., a Saturday might be a workday due to a holiday swap, while a Sunday might be a day off).

The current cron system only supports time-based triggers. It cannot handle such dynamic "pre-conditions" natively. As a workaround, I have to use an external shell script as a "guard" with the system crontab, which splits the configuration logic and increases maintenance overhead.

### Proposed Solution

I propose adding a `condition` field to cron jobs. This field would be evaluated **before** the main `task` executes. If the condition returns `false` or a non-zero exit code, the job is skipped entirely (no task execution, no notification).

To cover different use cases, the `condition` field could support two modes:

**Option 1 (Shell Command) — Recommended for efficiency:**
```yaml
cron:
  - name: "daily_briefing"
    schedule: "0 9 * * *"
    condition: "/path/to/check-workday.sh"  # Executed as a shell command
    task: "Generate and send today's briefing"
```
- The job is skipped if the shell command exits with a non-zero code.
- Zero token cost, fast, deterministic.

**Option 2 (Natural Language) — For complex, knowledge-based rules:**

```yaml
cron:
  - name: "daily_briefing"
    schedule: "0 9 * * *"
    condition: "Check if today is a workday, respecting Chinese statutory holidays and compensatory working days."
    task: "Generate and send today's briefing"
```

- The Agent evaluates the natural language statement via a lightweight LLM call.
- Skipped if the statement evaluates to false.


**Optional enhancement:**
Allow both to be combined (e.g., run shell command first; if it's not available or returns an "unknown" code, fall back to LLM evaluation).

This design gives users flexibility: deterministic checks via shell, intelligent checks via LLM, or a hybrid approach.
